module purpose: neorv32_twd is a bus-configured two-wire serial device block. Bus writes load control bits and transmit bytes, sampled twd_sda_i/twd_scl_i drive a transfer state machine that matches a programmed 7-bit address and exchanges bytes through RX/TX FIFOs, and the block drives twd_sda_o, reports status and received data on bus_rsp_o, exports clkgen_en_o, and raises irq_o.

use-case flows.value: control register fields written into held settings for enable, FIFO clear, sample-clock select, device address, interrupt enables, dummy-byte fallback, and read-hiding
a detected serial start condition begins a transfer by moving the engine from S_IDLE to S_INIT
sampled serial-line state and bus events derived from twd_sda_i/twd_scl_i using the selected clkgen_i tap
serial address, write data, and read-response bytes moved between the serial interface and the RX/TX paths
interrupt request generated from configured FIFO conditions
control/status fields and RX FIFO data returned on bus reads
control settings, backup transmit byte, sampler state, interrupt output, and engine state/outputs forced to known values while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.enable is written at line 159, read back at line 172, copied to clkgen_en_o at line 198, and gates FIFO clear, interrupt generation, sampling, and engine operation at lines 230, 281, 293, 315, 381, 389, 397, 421, 434, and 465. These flows depend on the exact stored enable value; availability is also established because the setting is held in ctrl.enable and exported on clkgen_en_o.

ctrl.fsel is written at line 162 and returned at line 173. It selects smp.clk_en between clkgen_i(clk_div64_c) and clkgen_i(clk_div8_c) at line 329, and smp.clk_en gates sampler updates and valid-sample generation at lines 316-319 and 317. Integrity of sampling cadence and the derived bus events depends on this selection.

ctrl.device_addr is written at line 163 and returned at line 174. In S_ADDR, line 402 compares ctrl.device_addr with engine.sreg(7 downto 1), and lines 404 and 406 use that comparison to decide whether the engine ignores the transaction or responds. Integrity of address acceptance depends on this stored 7-bit setting.

ctrl.hide_read and ctrl.tx_dummy_en are written at lines 168 and 167 and returned at lines 179 and 178. ctrl.hide_read participates in the matched-read suppression condition at lines 403-406, and ctrl.tx_dummy_en selects tx_dummy as the read-response source when tx_fifo has no data at lines 250-252. Integrity of read-side behavior depends on these stored policy bits; availability of a fallback response is established by the tx_dummy_en path.

ctrl.clr_rx and ctrl.clr_tx are forced low each cycle at lines 154-155, can be set by bus writes at lines 160-161, and directly drive rx_fifo.clr and tx_fifo.clr at lines 281 and 230. Integrity matters because unintended assertion clears buffered serial data, while availability is also established because these pulses are the implemented clear mechanism.

ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_rx_full, and ctrl.irq_tx_empty are written at lines 164-166, returned at lines 175-177, and are used in the irq_o expression at lines 293-296 together with FIFO status. Integrity of which FIFO conditions can raise irq_o depends on these stored bits.

The engine case statement at line 377 and the next-state assignments at lines 382, 390, 392, 398, 400, 404, 406, 422, 424, 435, 437, 441, 444, 466, 469, and 487 define the current protocol phase. engine.cnt increments on sampled clock rises at lines 413 and 450 and gates byte-complete actions at lines 401 and 438. engine.cmd captures the address LSB at line 420 and then steers receive/transmit behavior at lines 443, 453, 468, and 481. engine.ack captures the peer acknowledge bit at line 474 and affects continuation at lines 468-469. Integrity and availability of serial transaction sequencing depend on this stored control state.

twd_sda_i is sampled into smp.sda_sreg at line 311, and engine.sreg shifts in the sampled bit on sampled clock rises at lines 412 and 449. The resulting byte is used for address comparison at line 402, command capture at line 420, and RX FIFO writes through rx_fifo.wdata at line 282 when engine.wr_we is asserted at line 443. Integrity of received address and write-data bytes depends on this path; availability is established because the byte is held in engine.sreg until used.

tx_dummy stores the last tx_fifo.rdata byte when tx_fifo.avail and engine.rd_re are asserted at lines 241-242. engine.rdata then selects tx_fifo.rdata, tx_dummy, or all ones at lines 250-252; engine.dout loads the selected response bit at lines 429, 456, and 464; and twd_sda_o copies engine.dout during transmit at line 454. Integrity of bytes sent on the serial data output depends on these values, and availability is established by the fallback behavior in lines 250-252.

irq_o is registered at lines 292-296 from ctrl.enable and the enabled FIFO conditions. Integrity requires the reported interrupt request to match the configured conditions and current FIFO status; availability is also established because the output is driven every rising edge while reset is inactive.
engine.busy is computed at line 494 as '0' only when engine.state = S_IDLE and is returned on the status read path at line 188. Integrity of the reported busy/idle status depends on this decision.
